issues.title: Converge project identity to one Workspace id + version the SQLite run-store
issues.description:
## Objective
Execute the disposition matrix's "M1 — identity + persistence" milestone: converge the three
divergent project-identity derivations onto one Workspace id, and give the SQLite run-store
real versioned migrations with a SQLite/Postgres parity test.

## Desired outcome
Exactly one project/workspace identity derivation exists and is used everywhere state is
keyed; the SQLite run-store's schema lives in `lib/db/migrations/` (not an inline `CREATE
TABLE`), and a parity test proves SQLite and Postgres return equivalent run records for the
same operations.

## Locked architectural decision
`deriveProjectKey` (git-remote hash) is the canonical Workspace-identity derivation (target
concept 1). `orchestration/store.projectKey` and `embed/daemon.resolveRootDir` are rewritten to
read it rather than deriving independently. The SQLite run-store's schema becomes
version-1-controlled via the migration runner, reproducing the current inline schema exactly
(no behavior change, only a storage-shape rebuild — disposition-matrix.md verdict C2 "rebuild").

## Requirements
1. Rewrite `orchestration/store.projectKey` and `embed/daemon.resolveRootDir` to call the one
   canonical `deriveProjectKey`.
2. Assert one id across all three call sites (extend the existing
   `cross-process-state-has-one-authoritative-location` invariant test).
3. Reconcile any state currently stored under a divergent key (audit for stray state directories
   keyed by the two non-canonical derivations before deleting them).
4. Author `lib/db/migrations/` files reproducing the current inline SQLite run-store schema as
   version 1.
5. Add a backend-parity test asserting SQLite and Postgres return equivalent run records for the
   same write/read sequence (mirrors directive §4's day-one "equivalent results on SQLite and
   Postgres," applied here to run-store rather than the graph store).
6. Delete the inline `CREATE TABLE` code path in `run-store-sqlite.mjs` only after the migration
   runner owns the schema and the parity test is green.

## Acceptance criteria
- A single test asserts `deriveProjectKey`, `orchestration/store.projectKey`, and
  `embed/daemon.resolveRootDir` return the identical key for the same repo.
- `lib/db/migrations/` contains a run-store version-1 migration; `run-store-sqlite.mjs` no
  longer contains an inline `CREATE TABLE`.
- A parity test runs the same operation sequence against both backends and asserts equal
  results.
- `npm run test:unit` and `construct doctor` green.

## Context
Disposition-matrix.md duplication row D6 (project-identity ×3, **remove 2 of 3**) and Cluster C2
(run-store backends, **rebuild**). Matrix's own "Cleanup milestones § M1."

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/disposition-matrix.md] — D6 row
(~606), Cluster C2 (~291–309), M1 (~659–661).

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
No graph-store nodes affected (this is run-store, not the dependency graph); if project-identity
convergence touches any graph-store keying by project, re-run `construct graph reconcile` to
confirm no drift.

## Expected edge changes
None in the dependency graph proper.

## Impacted dependents
Every consumer of `orchestration/store.projectKey` or `embed/daemon.resolveRootDir` (state-root
resolution, `.construct/projects/<key>/` scoping) — a full-suite run after the rewrite is the
regression gate.

## Dependency rationale
None on other new beads in this program — this is foundational, evidence-grounded cleanup that
can start immediately alongside M0/M2.

## Non-goals
Does not touch the Postgres migration runner itself (already real, per C2's own evidence) — only
brings SQLite up to the same discipline. Does not attempt E7's shared-workspace server work;
this is local persistence hygiene only.

## Risks
Medium — rewriting identity derivation touches every state-root resolution path; a botched
migration could scope existing user state under a new key and orphan it. Mitigate with the
reconciliation-audit requirement (item 3) before any deletion of old-keyed state.

## Security
None beyond standard care around not silently losing user state during the identity/key
rewrite (data-loss risk, not a security vulnerability).

## Authority requirements
None — local persistence change, no external effect, no approval chokepoint.

## Implementation guidance
Do the identity convergence and the run-store migration as two independent, sequential steps
inside one bead (they touch different files but are grouped under one milestone per the
matrix); write the reconciliation audit script before touching any deletion.

## Required capabilities
Read/Grep/Edit/Bash; direct SQLite/Postgres access for the parity test.

## Recommended runtime and model capability
Mid-to-strong coding runtime — the identity-convergence rewrite has real regression risk across
many call sites and deserves careful review, not a cheap worker.

## Parallelization eligibility and rationale
The two halves (identity convergence; run-store migration) touch disjoint files and could run
as two workers, but are kept as one bead per the matrix's own grouping — split further only if a
future lead judges the integration overhead of doing them separately is worth it.

## Workspace/worktree ownership
One throwaway worktree off `feat/workspace-control-plane`.

## File ownership
`lib/orchestration/store.mjs`, `lib/embed/daemon.mjs`, `lib/paths.mjs` (or wherever
`deriveProjectKey` canonically lives), `lib/db/migrations/`, `lib/storage/run-store-sqlite.mjs`,
`lib/storage/backend-registry.mjs`. No conflict with M0's file set.

## Inputs
Disposition-matrix.md's D6/C2 evidence; the existing Postgres migration runner
(`lib/db/migrate.mjs`, `lib/db/migrations/001_orchestration_runs.sql`) as the pattern to mirror.

## Outputs
New migration file(s), a rewritten identity-derivation call graph, a new parity test.

## Integration contract
`orchestration/store.projectKey` and `embed/daemon.resolveRootDir`'s public signatures are
unchanged — only their internals now delegate to `deriveProjectKey`.

## Validation
The identity-equality test, the backend-parity test, full unit suite, `construct doctor`.

## Graph validation
`construct graph reconcile` clean (no drift attributable to this change).

## Migration
Run-store SQLite schema becomes version 1 in the migration runner, reproducing current schema
exactly — no data transformation needed, only a mechanism change. Any state found under a
divergent project key (item 3) is reconciled into the canonical key's location, not discarded.

## Rollback
Per the matrix's rollback plan: run-store migrations are additive (version 1 reproduces the
current inline schema), so reverting the migration files leaves data readable by the old inline
path; identity convergence keeps `deriveProjectKey` as the canonical it already is, so revert is
a no-op on stored keys.

## Deletion/cleanup
Delete the inline `CREATE TABLE` code path only after the migration runner owns the schema and
the parity test is green (per Requirements item 6).

## Completion evidence
Link the merge commit, the identity-equality test output, and the parity-test output.
issues.close_reason: Project identity converged onto deriveProjectKey; SQLite run-store versioned via lib/db/migrations/. ADR-0092. Merged into feat/workspace-control-plane.

issues.title: Formalize the governed-write pipeline as the sole authority chokepoint
issues.description:
## Objective
Execute the disposition matrix's "M2 — governance formalization" milestone (directive §17 E6):
declare the existing control-plane→ApprovalQueue→envelope→sent-log pipeline the single governed-
write chokepoint, fold in the two satellite approval recorders, and delete the one recorder that
becomes redundant.

## Desired outcome
Every external effect (provider write, destructive MCP tool call, workflow-driven mutation)
passes through exactly one authority/approval/idempotency chokepoint. `roles/approval-surface.mjs`
is deleted because its callers now route through the chokepoint directly.

## Locked architectural decision
Per disposition-matrix.md's narrowing 2 (A4 supported): the "five competing approval surfaces"
finding was wrong — three of five are already layers of one pipeline
(`control-plane.mjs`→`write-intent.mjs`→`ApprovalQueue`→`envelope.mjs`+`sent-log.mjs`). The
chokepoint is `control-plane.mjs`; it does not need to be rebuilt, only formalized and completed.
This *is* target concept 13 (Policy chokepoint) and directive §17 E6 in full.

## Requirements
1. Declare `control-plane.mjs` the single governed-write path in code/docs (a header-comment and
   an architecture-doc update, not a rewrite).
2. Wire `mcp/destructive-gate.mjs`'s `issueApprovalToken`/`consumeApprovalToken` to record token
   issuance in control-plane's authority store, so there is one authority ledger instead of a
   parallel one.
3. Route `roles/approval-surface.mjs`'s three consumers (`hooks/edit-guard`, `hooks/guard-bash`,
   `embedded-contract/workflow-invoke`) through the chokepoint directly.
4. Delete `roles/approval-surface.mjs` once all three consumers are migrated and zero remaining
   callers exist.
5. Migrate any per-surface idempotency logic found in the three consumers to the envelope's
   existing idempotency/dedup/retry/audit machinery, rather than keeping a second idempotency
   implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
- `grep -rn "roles/approval-surface"` returns zero hits outside the deletion commit's own diff.
- A single authority-ledger test asserts both a provider-write approval and an MCP
  destructive-tool-token approval are recorded in the same store.
- `npm run test:unit`, `construct doctor`, and the no-skip-vars hook test all green (this
  chokepoint is exactly the kind of gate CLAUDE.md's no-skip-vars rule protects).

## Context
Disposition-matrix.md Cluster E1g/E2g (**retain**, **retain+reconcile**) and duplication row D1
(narrowed High→Medium). Matrix's own "Cleanup milestones § M2." This bead is also the concrete
content of directive §17's E6 ("policies, approvals, and effects — authority, policy, approval,
revalidation, leases, idempotency, transactional outbox, external verification, GitHub/Jira
effects").

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/disposition-matrix.md] — Cluster
E1g/E2g (~495–527), D1 narrowing (~89–102), M2 (~662–663).

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
No dependency-graph nodes change; this is a runtime authority/approval mechanism, not a graph
artifact.

## Expected edge changes
None in the dependency graph.

## Impacted dependents
`hooks/edit-guard`, `hooks/guard-bash`, `embedded-contract/workflow-invoke` (rewired), every
provider governed-write path and the MCP destructive-tool flow (must remain green throughout).

## Dependency rationale
None on other new beads — this can start immediately, in parallel with M0/M1. It is itself a
precondition (per the matrix's own point-of-no-return note) for M3's daemon/routing
consolidation: M3 must not begin "until... the D1/A4 chokepoint (M2) is proven to have zero
write-path bypass."

## Non-goals
Does not touch the graph, run-store, or org-metaphor subsystems. Does not add new governed-write
capability — only consolidates the authority ledger for what already exists.

## Risks
Medium-high — this gates every external effect in the system; a bug here has the highest blast
radius of any M0-M2 bead. Mitigate with the no-skip-vars test suite and a staged rollout: wire
the MCP token-gate authority recording first (additive, low-risk), delete
`roles/approval-surface.mjs` only after all three consumers are proven migrated.

## Security
This *is* the security-relevant chokepoint — the whole point is a single, auditable authority
ledger instead of two. No new attack surface; consolidation should reduce it (fewer places an
approval can be silently bypassed).

## Authority requirements
This bead touches the authority/approval mechanism itself. Any change here should be reviewed
against `rules/common/commit-approval.md`-equivalent rigor even though it is not itself a
commit-approval change — i.e., extra scrutiny before merge, not a special external approval.

## Implementation guidance
Do the additive step (wire MCP token authority into control-plane's ledger) first and prove it
green before touching the destructive step (deleting `roles/approval-surface.mjs`), so a bug in
the additive step doesn't compound with a deletion.

## Required capabilities
Read/Grep/Edit/Bash; access to run the full governed-write test surface.

## Recommended runtime and model capability
Strongest available coding runtime — this is the highest-blast-radius bead in the M0-M2 tier and
should not be a cheap-worker task.

## Parallelization eligibility and rationale
Low — the additive wiring and the consumer migration are sequentially dependent (can't delete
`approval-surface.mjs` before its three consumers are migrated), so this is a single-worker,
single-sequence bead, not a fan-out candidate. Matches the matrix's own "never fan out" spirit
for governance-shaped work even though this specific bead isn't WS5/WS6.

## Workspace/worktree ownership
One dedicated worktree off `feat/workspace-control-plane`, not shared with M0/M1 (different
concern, avoids any accidental cross-contamination of a governance-critical change).

## File ownership
`lib/writes/control-plane.mjs`, `write-intent.mjs`, `envelope.mjs`, `sent-log.mjs`,
`lib/embed/approval-queue.mjs`, `lib/mcp/destructive-approval.mjs`, `destructive-gate.mjs`,
`lib/roles/approval-surface.mjs`, `lib/hooks/edit-guard.mjs`, `guard-bash.mjs`,
`lib/embedded-contract/workflow-invoke.mjs`.

## Inputs
Disposition-matrix.md's D1/A4 narrowing (already-gathered evidence); the existing chokepoint
code as the base to formalize, not rebuild.

## Outputs
A documented single chokepoint, one authority ledger, three rewired consumers, one deleted
module.

## Integration contract
`hooks/edit-guard`/`guard-bash`/`workflow-invoke`'s calls into the (soon-deleted)
`approval-surface.recordApprovalRequest` are replaced with calls into the chokepoint's
equivalent function — same semantic guarantee (an approval is recorded before the guarded action
proceeds), different call target.

## Validation
Full unit suite, `construct doctor`, no-skip-vars hook test, the new authority-ledger test.

## Graph validation
Not applicable (no graph-store change).

## Migration
Reconcile `.construct/…/routing/` or any approval-surface-specific state into the control-plane
authority store before deleting `approval-surface.mjs` — no approval history should be silently
lost.

## Rollback
Per the matrix's rollback plan (M2 is pre-point-of-no-return): `git revert` per step; the
additive MCP-token-ledger wiring is safe to revert on its own, and `approval-surface.mjs`'s
deletion should be the last, most-reversible-checked step.

## Deletion/cleanup
Delete `roles/approval-surface.mjs` only after zero remaining callers are confirmed (see
Requirements item 4).

## Completion evidence
Link the merge commit, the authority-ledger test output, and a `grep` confirming zero remaining
`approval-surface` references outside history.
issues.close_reason: Governed-write pipeline formalized as sole chokepoint with shared authority ledger; roles/approval-surface.mjs deleted. Merged into feat/workspace-control-plane.

issues.title: Consolidate roles routing into orchestration/routing-tables
issues.description:
## Objective
Fold the roles layer's routing primitives (`roles/router.mjs`, `roles/gateway.mjs`) into
`orchestration/routing-tables.mjs`, resolving duplication row D4 — the first half of the
disposition matrix's "M3 — routing + daemon consolidation" milestone.

## Desired outcome
One routing implementation (`orchestration/routing-tables`) decides event→persona/worker
routing; `roles/router.mjs`/`gateway.mjs` are deleted once every caller (including the Oracle
daemon, until M3b replaces it) routes through the consolidated table.

## Locked architectural decision
Per disposition-matrix.md narrowing 1: `roles/router.mjs` is NOT dead — `route()` is called by
`gateway.mjs:257`, and `gateway.recordAndMaybeInvoke` is called live by `oracle/execute.mjs:65`.
This is a **replace via consolidation**, not a deletion of dead code. The `event-bus.mjs` signal
backbone (5 live importers) is *rehomed*, not deleted, per the matrix's replacement-strategy
table ("Parallel next-generation → direct cutover... Preserve event-bus + contracts across the
seam").

## Requirements
1. Merge `roles/router.mjs`'s routing logic into `orchestration/routing-tables.mjs` so there is
   one routing-table implementation.
2. Rewire `roles/gateway.mjs`'s callers (`oracle/execute.mjs:65` today, superseded by M3b's
   consolidated overseer) to call the consolidated routing table directly.
3. Preserve `roles/event-bus.mjs` as-is (or move it, keeping its public API) — it has 5 live
   importers (`embed/recommendation-store`, `embed/docs-lifecycle`, `intake/prepare`,
   `hooks/agent-tracker`, `scopes/lifecycle`) that must not break.
4. Delete `roles/router.mjs` and `roles/gateway.mjs` only after their sole caller
   (`oracle/execute.mjs`) is itself replaced by M3b's consolidated overseer — this bead prepares
   the target; M3b's daemon cutover is what removes the last caller.

## Acceptance criteria
- A routing-equivalence test asserts the consolidated `orchestration/routing-tables` produces
  the same routing decision as the current `roles/router.route()` for a representative event
  set.
- `event-bus.mjs`'s 5 importers pass their existing tests unchanged.
- `npm run test:unit` and `construct doctor` green.
- `roles/router.mjs`/`gateway.mjs` are NOT yet deleted at the end of this bead (that happens once
  M3b removes their last caller) — this bead's AC is "routing consolidated and equivalence
  proven," not "old files gone."

## Context
Disposition-matrix.md Cluster C4 (roles layer, **replace**) and duplication row D4 (routing
layers). Matrix's own "Cleanup milestones § M3" (routing half).

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/disposition-matrix.md] — Cluster
C4 (~327–355), D4 row (~604), M3 (~664–666), point-of-no-return note (~673–684).

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
None directly (routing is a runtime mechanism, not a graph artifact) — `specialist` node type
migration (→ `worker profile`) is M4's concern, not this bead's.

## Expected edge changes
None in the dependency graph.

## Impacted dependents
`event-bus.mjs`'s 5 importers (must remain green); `oracle/execute.mjs` (temporarily still calls
the old gateway until M3b cuts it over).

## Dependency rationale
Depends on M2 (governance chokepoint proven) per the matrix's explicit point-of-no-return
precondition: "do not begin M3 until... (b) the D1/A4 chokepoint (M2) is proven to have zero
write-path bypass." This bead is the lower-risk half of M3 and can start once M2 is green,
without waiting for M3b's Oracle-daemon cutover (which additionally needs E5's production
workplace loop).

## Non-goals
Does not delete `roles/router.mjs`/`gateway.mjs` (M3b's job, gated on the daemon cutover). Does
not touch `event-bus.mjs`'s implementation, only preserves its call surface.

## Risks
High — this is inside the point-of-no-return window the matrix names. A routing-equivalence
regression would silently misroute events. Mitigate with the equivalence test as a hard gate
before any deletion.

## Security
None new — routing decisions are internal dispatch, not an external-effect boundary (that's
M2's concern, already formalized).

## Authority requirements
None beyond standard merge review given the point-of-no-return status.

## Implementation guidance
Build the consolidated routing table beside the existing `roles/router`, prove equivalence, then
switch callers over one at a time (not a big-bang cutover) — matches the matrix's own "Parallel
next-generation → direct cutover" strategy for this cluster.

## Required capabilities
Read/Grep/Edit/Bash; ability to run the full orchestration test surface.

## Recommended runtime and model capability
Strongest available coding runtime — point-of-no-return-adjacent work, same caution tier as M2.

## Parallelization eligibility and rationale
Low — routing consolidation is a single coherent piece of surgery, not fan-out-friendly. One
worker, sequential steps (build parallel table → prove equivalence → switch callers).

## Workspace/worktree ownership
One dedicated worktree off `feat/workspace-control-plane`.

## File ownership
`lib/roles/router.mjs`, `gateway.mjs`, `event-bus.mjs`, `lib/orchestration/routing-tables.mjs`.
No conflict with M2's file set (different modules within roles/orchestration).

## Inputs
Disposition-matrix.md's D4/C4 evidence; the existing `orchestration/routing-tables.mjs` as the
consolidation target.

## Outputs
A consolidated routing implementation; an equivalence test; `event-bus.mjs` preserved unchanged.

## Integration contract
Callers of `roles/gateway.recordAndMaybeInvoke` get an equivalent routing decision whether they
call the old gateway or (once cut over) the consolidated table directly — same semantic contract,
different implementation location.

## Validation
The routing-equivalence test, full unit suite, `construct doctor`.

## Graph validation
Not applicable.

## Migration
None — routing decisions are not durable state; no data migration needed, only a call-graph
change.

issues.title: Consolidate Oracle daemon into embed daemon, then delete the Oracle entity
issues.description:
## Objective
Consolidate the Oracle daemon into the embed daemon (the survivor per disposition-matrix.md
Cluster B1/B2), migrating Oracle's non-duplicative jobs to their new owners, then delete the
Oracle daemon entity — the second half of "M3 — routing + daemon consolidation."

## Desired outcome
One overseer daemon (embed) runs the union of both daemons' non-duplicative jobs.
`lib/oracle/daemon-entry.mjs` and `doctor/watchers/oracle-liveness.mjs` are deleted;
`.construct/oracle/` state is reconciled into its new owners, not silently dropped.

## Locked architectural decision
Oracle is **replaced**, not removed outright: its capabilities (directive execution,
reconciliation) survive under new owners. `directive-executor.mjs` re-homes under E5 (workplace
loop); read-model reconciliation re-homes under E1 (graph, already largely built by
construct-b0nny.3). The embed daemon is the survivor because it is already the more-wired
overseer (8 importers, ~11 job families, interval scheduler, write-intent drain).

## Requirements
1. Re-home `directive-executor.mjs` under the E5 workplace-loop bead's ownership.
2. Re-home read-model reconciliation under E1 (the relational graph store,
   `lib/graph/relational/reconcile.mjs`).
3. Route remediation dispatch through the M2 governed-write chokepoint.
4. Keep the roles-gateway call path (via M3a's consolidated routing) until Oracle's daemon-entry
   is deleted.
5. Delete `lib/oracle/daemon-entry.mjs` and `doctor/watchers/oracle-liveness.mjs` only after: (a)
   directive execution runs under E5 with equivalent tests green, (b) reconciliation runs under
   E1, (c) zero remaining importers of `lib/oracle/read-model.mjs` outside migrated code, (d)
   `construct dev`/`service-manager` no longer starts `runOracleDaemon`.
6. Reconcile `.construct/oracle/` state (pending, raised-issues, verdicts, routing) into the
   E5/E1 stores before removing the directory.

## Acceptance criteria
- The embed daemon runs directive execution and reconciliation with tests equivalent to
  Oracle's current coverage.
- `grep -rn "runOracleDaemon\|oracle/daemon-entry\|oracle-liveness"` returns zero hits outside
  history after deletion.
- `.construct/oracle/` state is reconciled (a migration script + its own test), not silently
  lost.
- `npm run test:unit`, `construct doctor` green; the four gating conditions in Requirements
  item 5 are each individually demonstrated in the PR description.

## Context
Disposition-matrix.md Cluster B1 (embed daemon, **retain** as survivor)/B2 (Oracle, **replace**)
and duplication row D3. Matrix's own point-of-no-return note names this bead's preconditions
explicitly.

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/disposition-matrix.md] — Cluster
B1/B2 (~219–257), D3 row (~603), point-of-no-return (~673–684).

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
None new; the reconciliation logic being re-homed already exists in `lib/graph/relational/`
(construct-b0nny.3) and is not re-invented here.

## Expected edge changes
None.

## Impacted dependents
Everything currently watching Oracle liveness (`doctor/watchers/oracle-liveness.mjs`) or
consuming `oracle/read-model.mjs` — each must have a proven equivalent before deletion.

## Dependency rationale
Depends on M2 (chokepoint proven), M3a (routing consolidated, so the last gateway caller has
somewhere to route to), and the new E5 bead (workplace loop must exist and pass equivalence
tests before Oracle's directive-execution job can be safely deleted) — this is the actual
point-of-no-return gate the matrix names.

## Non-goals
Does not build E5's workplace loop from scratch (that is E5's own bead) — this bead only
migrates Oracle's directive-execution *job* onto whatever E5 builds, once E5 is green.

## Risks
High — named point-of-no-return in the matrix. A missed Oracle capability becomes a silent
regression once the daemon is deleted. Mitigate with the four explicit gating conditions and the
config-declared rollback seam (see Rollback).

## Security
None new.

## Authority requirements
None beyond standard high-caution merge review for a point-of-no-return change.

## Implementation guidance
Do not delete the Oracle daemon-entry until all four gating conditions are independently
demonstrated — this is the single most important discipline in the whole program, per the
matrix's own explicit warning.

## Required capabilities
Read/Grep/Edit/Bash; ability to run the daemon supervision test surface.

## Recommended runtime and model capability
Strongest available coding runtime — highest-risk single bead in the program.

## Parallelization eligibility and rationale
Low — sequential by nature (migrate job A, prove it, migrate job B, prove it, then delete).

## Workspace/worktree ownership
One dedicated worktree off `feat/workspace-control-plane`.

## File ownership
`lib/oracle/**`, `lib/embed/daemon.mjs`, `doctor/watchers/oracle-liveness.mjs`,
`lib/service-manager.mjs` (daemon start/stop wiring). No conflict with M3a's file set.

## Inputs
M3a's consolidated routing; the E5 bead's production workplace loop; construct-b0nny.3's graph
reconciliation.

## Outputs
One consolidated overseer daemon; Oracle's daemon-entry and liveness watcher deleted;
`.construct/oracle/` state reconciled.

## Integration contract
Any caller of Oracle's public functions (`directive-executor`, `read-model`) gets equivalent
behavior from the new owner (E5, E1) — same semantic guarantee, different module.

## Validation
Equivalence tests for directive execution and reconciliation; full unit suite; `construct
doctor`; the four explicit gating-condition checks.

## Graph validation
`construct graph reconcile` clean post-migration.

## Migration
`.construct/oracle/` state (pending, raised-issues, verdicts, routing) reconciled into the E5/E1
stores — a migration script with its own test, not a silent drop.

## Rollback
Per the matrix's rollback plan: keep the Oracle daemon-entry and roles router behind a
config-declared overseer-selection seam for one release after cutover; delete the seam and old
code only in the *following* release once the consolidated overseer has run clean in production.

## Deletion/cleanup
`lib/oracle/daemon-entry.mjs`, `doctor/watchers/oracle-liveness.mjs`, and (once M3a's last
caller is gone) `roles/router.mjs`/`gateway.mjs` — see Requirements item 5 for the exact gating.

## Completion evidence
Link the merge commit; paste each of the four gating-condition proofs; link the
`.construct/oracle/` reconciliation script's test output.

issues.title: Migrate org metaphor (scopes/personas/teams) into Worker Profiles
issues.description:
## Objective
Execute the disposition matrix's "M4 — org-metaphor cutover": migrate `specialists/org/scopes/`
into Worker Profiles (target concept 10), fold personas into skill-emphasis inputs, retire
teams/groups as fixed structure, and preserve handoff contracts + capability registry.

## Desired outcome
Parallelism is expressed as a Plan property (directive §10), not a fixed team; a Worker Profile
(flow + skill emphasis) replaces the persona/role/specialist/team scaffolding.
`specialists/org/contracts/` and `registry/capabilities.json` survive unchanged.

## Locked architectural decision
Per disposition-matrix.md Cluster F3 (**replace**) and target-model.md concept 10: a Profile is
"a flow + skill emphasis," not an organizational identity. Handoff contracts and the capability
registry are the load-bearing parts and are retained; the metaphor scaffolding (teams, groups,
separate persona identities) is replaced.

## Requirements
1. Follow the existing profile lifecycle (`docs/guides/concepts/profile-lifecycle.md`,
   `construct scope create`) to migrate each of the 4 scopes into a Worker Profile.
2. Fold personas into skill-emphasis inputs rather than standalone identity files.
3. Retire `specialists/org/teams/`/`groups/` once Plans express parallelism directly (directive
   §10) and no flow references a team.
4. Regenerate platform files via `construct sync` so deleted personas leave no generated
   residue (program rule 2: "every replacement carries its deletion").
5. Keep `specialists/org/contracts/` and `registry/capabilities.json` untouched.

## Acceptance criteria
- All 4 scopes have a corresponding Worker Profile passing the profile-lifecycle's own
  validation gate.
- `grep -rn` for team/group references in any live flow returns zero hits before
  `specialists/org/teams/`/`groups/` are deleted.
- `construct sync` run after deletion leaves no stale generated persona files.
- `npm run test:unit`, `construct doctor` green.

## Context
Disposition-matrix.md Cluster F3 (~568–590), replacement-strategy row "Roles + org metaphor"
(~634), Cleanup milestones § M4 (~667–668); target-model.md concept 10 (Worker Profile).

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/disposition-matrix.md] Cluster F3;
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/target-model.md] concept 10.

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
`specialist` node type migrates to `worker profile` (target concept 10's own migration note).

## Expected edge changes
`owned_by` edges currently pointing at specialist nodes re-point at worker-profile nodes.

## Impacted dependents
`specialists/org/contracts/` postcondition enforcement (CLAUDE.md) — must keep resolving against
whatever now owns handoffs; anything reading persona identity directly.

## Dependency rationale
Depends on M3a (Worker Profile routing rides on the consolidated `orchestration/routing-tables`,
not the old roles router) — cutting over the org metaphor before routing is consolidated would
create two migrations touching the same seam at once.

## Non-goals
Does not touch `specialists/org/contracts/` or `registry/capabilities.json` — both explicitly
retained. Does not redesign the profile-lifecycle process itself (already documented).

## Risks
Medium — persona/team deletion could silently break a flow that still references a team by name.
Mitigate with the pre-deletion grep gate (Requirements item 3/AC).

## Security
None new.

## Authority requirements
None beyond standard merge review; this is a repo-content migration, not a runtime authority
change.

## Implementation guidance
Follow `profile-lifecycle.md`'s discover→frame→emphasize→validate→promote sequence per scope,
rather than inventing a new migration process — CLAUDE.md already mandates this lifecycle for
any new profile.

## Required capabilities
Read/Grep/Edit/Bash; `construct scope create`/`construct sync` CLI access.

## Recommended runtime and model capability
Mid-to-strong — profile design benefits from real judgment (per profile-lifecycle.md, "research
artifacts, not JSON exercises"), but the migration itself is mechanical once profiles exist.

## Parallelization eligibility and rationale
The 4 scope migrations are independent of each other (different scope files) and could run in
parallel, but the final teams/groups retirement is a single integration step gating all of them
— structure as fan-out-then-integrate if desired by whoever executes this bead.

## Workspace/worktree ownership
One worktree off `feat/workspace-control-plane`, or 4 short-lived worktrees for the scope
migrations plus one for final integration.

## File ownership
`specialists/org/scopes/`, `specialists/org/teams/`, `specialists/org/groups/`, `personas/*.md`.
Explicitly NOT `specialists/org/contracts/` or `registry/capabilities.json`.

## Inputs
target-model.md's Worker Profile schema (concept 10); the existing profile-lifecycle process.

## Outputs
4 Worker Profiles; retired teams/groups; regenerated platform files with no stale persona
residue.

## Integration contract
Handoff contracts continue to resolve the same way — only what they resolve *against* (Worker
Profile instead of persona/specialist) changes.

## Validation
Profile-lifecycle's own validation gate per profile; the pre-deletion team/group reference grep;
full unit suite; `construct doctor`.

## Graph validation
`construct graph orphans` clean after the `specialist`→`worker profile` node-type migration.

## Migration
`specialists/org/scopes/*.json` → Worker Profiles; personas → skill-emphasis inputs — both are
explicit "migrated data" entries in the disposition matrix's replacement-strategy table, not
silent drops.

## Rollback
Per the matrix's rollback plan: Worker Profiles are authored *beside* the scopes/personas before
deletion; rollback re-points selection at the retained scope files until profiles are validated.
No persona data is deleted until migrated.

## Deletion/cleanup
`specialists/org/teams/`/`groups/` deleted only after Plans express parallelism directly and no
flow references a team (Requirements item 3).

## Completion evidence
Link the merge commit; the 4 profile-lifecycle validation results; the `construct sync` output
showing no stale residue.

issues.title: Migrate model invocation/routing off model-router onto runtime adapters
issues.description:
## Objective
Migrate model invocation/routing off the bespoke `model-router.mjs` loop onto the E4
runtime-adapter contract, per disposition-matrix.md Cluster D2s (**replace**, E4-gated) — the
first half of "M5 — model-loop + vector de-core."

## Desired outcome
Model invocation/routing is delegated to runtime adapters (directive §3: Construct delegates
model invocation/routing to runtimes). Model capability-tier/policy metadata
(`model-tiers`/`model-policy`/`model-pricing`) survives as Worker Profile input
(`model_tier`); the routing/dispatch loop itself is deleted.

## Locked architectural decision
This is a **split** verdict: the invocation/routing *loop* is replaced (deleted once migrated);
the tier/policy *metadata* is retained and folds into Worker Profile's `model_tier` (target
concept 10). Construct still decides *which tier* a Profile needs; it stops owning *how* the call
is routed.

## Requirements
1. Build/confirm the E4 runtime-adapter contract exists and has a conformance suite (this bead
   depends on the E4 bead's output, not on redesigning it here).
2. Migrate the ≥16 importers of `model-router.mjs` (or its exported surface) onto the E4 runtime
   contract, one at a time, not big-bang.
3. Keep `model-tiers`/`model-policy`/`model-pricing` as retained metadata, re-homed as Worker
   Profile `model_tier` inputs.
4. Retire `model-registry.mjs` (a 501-byte stub with no real registry behavior).
5. Delete `model-router.mjs`'s routing/dispatch path only after every importer resolves model
   invocation through an E4 runtime adapter.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every former `model-router.mjs` importer now resolves invocation through an E4 adapter,
  verified by an equivalence test per migrated call site (or a representative sample if ≥16 is
  impractical to cover individually — state which sites were sampled and why).
- `model-tiers`/`model-policy`/`model-pricing` tests still pass, now reading as Worker Profile
  input.
- `grep -rn "model-router"` (routing/dispatch path only, not the retained metadata files) returns
  zero hits after deletion.
- `npm run test:unit`, `construct doctor` green.

## Context
Disposition-matrix.md Cluster D2s (~405–427), replacement-strategy row "Model/provider loop"
(~635, "Highest-risk seam; keep tier/policy metadata"). Directive §17 E9 lists "model-provider
loop deletion" as a named outcome.

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/disposition-matrix.md] Cluster
D2s; spike F's b0nny.5.6 report (a real, if narrower, runtime-adapter swap already proven safe
for one provider adapter) [source:
docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/spike-f-runtime-replacement.md].

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
None new; `provider`/`tool` nodes unaffected — this is invocation routing, not provider identity.

## Expected edge changes
None in the dependency graph.

## Impacted dependents
≥16 modules referencing `model-router` (truth-map §7 estimate; matrix notes a looser 25-file
grep count) — the highest-risk migration surface in the program per the matrix's own framing.

## Dependency rationale
Depends on the new E4 bead (runtime-adapter contract + conformance suite must exist first). Does
not depend on M0-M4 — can run in parallel with them once E4 is ready.

## Non-goals
Does not touch provider/contract adapters themselves (D1s, already retained) — only the
invocation/routing loop that decides which runtime handles a call.

## Risks
High — matrix's own words, "Highest-risk seam." A migration bug here could misroute every model
call in the system. Mitigate with per-importer equivalence tests and a parallel-run period before
deletion (matches spike F's proven pattern of shipping the new path beside the old one).

## Security
None new beyond the general care any invocation-path change deserves.

## Authority requirements
None beyond standard high-caution review given the risk tier.

## Implementation guidance
Follow spike F's proven pattern (b0nny.5.6): build the new path beside the old one, prove
equivalence per call site, migrate incrementally, keep a config-declared rollback seam, delete
last.

## Required capabilities
Read/Grep/Edit/Bash; access to run the model-invocation test surface across all migrated call
sites.

## Recommended runtime and model capability
Strongest available coding runtime — matrix-flagged highest-risk seam in the whole program.

## Parallelization eligibility and rationale
The ≥16 importers can migrate in parallel batches (independent call sites) once the E4 adapter
exists, but the final deletion of `model-router.mjs`'s routing path is a single integration step
gating all batches.

## Workspace/worktree ownership
One or more worktrees off `feat/workspace-control-plane`, one per migration batch if
parallelized.

## File ownership
`lib/model-router.mjs`, `model-policy.mjs`, `model-tiers.mjs`, `model-free-selector.mjs`,
`model-cheapest-provider.mjs`, `model-pricing.mjs`, `model-registry.mjs`, plus each of the ≥16
importer files (enumerate before starting to avoid silent scope creep).

## Inputs
The E4 runtime-adapter contract and conformance suite; spike F's proven swap pattern.

## Outputs
≥16 call sites migrated; retained tier/policy metadata re-homed as Worker Profile input;
`model-router.mjs`'s routing path and `model-registry.mjs` deleted.

## Integration contract
Every migrated call site gets equivalent model-invocation behavior via the E4 adapter contract
instead of the bespoke loop — same semantic guarantee (a model call happens with the right
tier/capability), different implementation.

## Validation
Per-call-site equivalence tests (or a justified representative sample); full unit suite;
`construct doctor`.

## Graph validation
Not applicable.

## Migration
Tier/policy metadata migrates to Worker Profile `model_tier` inputs — an explicit "migrated data"
entry, not a silent drop.

## Rollback
Per the matrix's rollback plan: the runtime-adapter path ships in parallel with `model-router`; a
config-declared runtime selection lets a bad adapter roll back to the bespoke loop for one
release.

## Deletion/cleanup
Delete `model-router.mjs`'s routing/dispatch path and `model-registry.mjs` only after every
importer is migrated and proven equivalent (Requirements item 5).

## Completion evidence
Link the merge commit; the per-call-site (or sampled) equivalence-test results; a `grep`
confirming zero remaining routing-path references.
issues.close_reason: Migrated model-router.mjs's 2 real invocation sites (intent-classifier, schema-infer) onto E4 claude-api adapter; honestly documented as partial since model-router.mjs contains no dispatch loop. Merged into feat/workspace-control-plane.

issues.title: De-core LanceDB behind an optional retrieval adapter with a no-vector fallback
issues.description:
## Objective
Move LanceDB behind an optional retrieval-adapter contract with a no-vector (keyword/BM25)
fallback, so the embedded/core product runs without a required vector database — disposition-
matrix.md Cluster D6s (**replace**), the second half of "M5 — model-loop + vector de-core."

## Desired outcome
Core Construct runs with no required vector DB (directive §13). LanceDB becomes one retrieval
adapter among possible others; a no-vector fallback passes the same memory tests.

## Locked architectural decision
The memory *domain model* (observation/entity store, D4s) is unaffected and stays retained —
only the *storage backend* is de-cored. `.construct/lancedb/observations_v1.lance` data is
re-indexed behind the adapter, never dropped.

## Requirements
1. Introduce a retrieval-adapter contract (interface for "given a query, return ranked memory
   hits") that LanceDB implements as one adapter.
2. Provide a no-vector fallback (keyword/BM25) implementing the same contract.
3. Re-index existing `.construct/lancedb/` data behind the adapter boundary (no silent data
   loss).
4. Remove the hard LanceDB import from core only after the adapter contract lands and the
   no-vector path passes the existing memory test suite.

## Acceptance criteria
- The existing observation/entity memory test suite passes against both the LanceDB adapter and
  the no-vector fallback.
- `grep -rn "lancedb"` outside the new adapter module returns zero hits in core code paths after
  cutover.
- A re-indexing script + test proves no data loss from `.construct/lancedb/`.
- `npm run test:unit`, `construct doctor` green.

## Context
Disposition-matrix.md Cluster D6s (~477–491), replacement-strategy row "Memory backend"
(~636, "Compatibility-backed").

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/disposition-matrix.md] Cluster
D6s.

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
None — memory nodes (D4s) are backed by this storage, not defined by it.

## Expected edge changes
None.

## Impacted dependents
Every consumer of `memory_search`/`knowledge_search` and the observation/entity store (D4s,
D5s) — must pass identically against either backend.

## Dependency rationale
Independent of M0-M4 and of E4/model-loop work — can run fully in parallel with everything else
in this program.

## Non-goals
Does not redesign the observation/entity domain model (D4s, retained as-is). Does not remove
LanceDB entirely — it remains a valid, first-class adapter, just no longer required.

## Risks
Medium — a re-indexing bug could lose or corrupt existing memory data. Mitigate with the
explicit "no silent data loss" acceptance criterion and a re-indexing dry-run mode.

## Security
None new.

## Authority requirements
None — local storage change, no external effect.

## Implementation guidance
Build the adapter contract and no-vector fallback first, prove both green against the existing
test suite, then do the re-index as a separate, reversible step before removing the hard import.

## Required capabilities
Read/Grep/Edit/Bash; ability to run the full memory/retrieval test surface.

## Recommended runtime and model capability
Mid-to-strong coding runtime; moderate risk, well-scoped.

## Parallelization eligibility and rationale
Fully parallel-safe with the rest of the program — touches a self-contained subsystem (memory
storage backend) with no shared file ownership with M0-M5a or the E-outcome beads.

## Workspace/worktree ownership
One worktree off `feat/workspace-control-plane`.

## File ownership
`lib/storage/vector-client.mjs`, `lib/storage/embeddings-*.mjs`, new retrieval-adapter contract
module, `.construct/lancedb/` re-indexing script.

## Inputs
Directive §13's "no required vector database" constraint; the existing observation/entity memory
test suite as the equivalence bar.

## Outputs
A retrieval-adapter contract; a no-vector fallback implementation; a re-indexing script; LanceDB
demoted from hard dependency to optional adapter.

## Integration contract
`memory_search`/`knowledge_search` callers see no interface change — only the backend behind
them becomes swappable.

## Validation
Full memory test suite against both backends; the re-indexing dry-run + real-run test.

## Graph validation
Not applicable.

## Migration
`.construct/lancedb/` data re-indexed behind the adapter — explicit "migrated data," never
dropped, per the matrix's own replacement-strategy table.

## Rollback
Per the matrix's rollback plan: the LanceDB adapter ships with the no-vector fallback already
green, so de-coring the vector DB is reversible by re-selecting the LanceDB adapter;
`.construct/lancedb/` data is re-indexed, never dropped.

## Deletion/cleanup
Remove the hard LanceDB import from core (Requirements item 4) only after the gating conditions
are met — LanceDB itself is not deleted, only its required-ness.

## Completion evidence
Link the merge commit; the dual-backend test results; the re-indexing proof.
issues.close_reason: LanceDB de-cored behind retrieval-adapter contract with BM25 keyword fallback; lancedb/apache-arrow now optionalDependencies. ADR-0081. Merged into feat/workspace-control-plane.

issues.title: Expose queryUp/queryDown via CLI + prove real Postgres graph parity
issues.description:
## Objective
Close the two concrete gaps spike A (construct-b0nny.5.1) found in the E1 graph foundation
beyond the recursive-CTE hang already tracked as construct-b0nny.12: `queryUp`/`queryDown` exist
in `lib/graph/relational/queries.mjs` but have no CLI subcommand exposing them, and Postgres
parity is still structural-only (never run against a live Postgres instance).

## Desired outcome
`construct graph` exposes `queryUp`/`queryDown` (directive §4.8 "query up/downstream") as real
commands, and Postgres parity is proven against a live Postgres instance at least once, not just
structurally mirrored SQL.

## Locked architectural decision
No new design — this is closing gaps in the already-designed and already-built relational graph
store (construct-b0nny.2/.3). Nothing about the store's shape changes here.

## Requirements
1. Add CLI subcommands (or extend `construct graph query`) exposing `queryUp`/`queryDown` with
   the rel-filter + depth-cap fix from construct-b0nny.12 applied.
2. Stand up a real Postgres instance (Docker Compose, per directive §17 E7's own deployment
   image work — coordinate with that bead rather than duplicating the setup) and run the day-one
   milestone functional tests against it.
3. Document the honest result either way — if Postgres parity holds, upgrade the "structural
   only" disclosure in `tests/functional/graph-relational-store.functional.test.mjs`'s
   documentation to "proven"; if it doesn't, file the gap as its own bead.

## Acceptance criteria
- `construct graph queryUp <id>`/`queryDown <id>` (or equivalent) work from the CLI with the
  b0nny.12 rel-filter/depth-cap applied.
- The 12 day-one milestone tests pass against a live Postgres instance at least once, with the
  run logged as real evidence (not simulated).
- `npm run test:unit`, `construct doctor` green.

## Context
Spike A (construct-b0nny.5.1) explicitly found: "`queryUp`/`queryDown` are exported from
`queries.mjs` but are not called from any CLI subcommand or any other `lib/` module today... the
directive §4.8 'query up/downstream' milestone capability exists as a function but has no exposed
command surface yet," and Postgres/Node<22.5 were both honestly disclosed as unverified in this
environment.

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/spike-a-graph-foundation.md].

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
None — this exposes existing query functions, doesn't add graph schema.

## Expected edge changes
None.

## Impacted dependents
Any future E7 (shared workspace) work that needs a real, tested Postgres backend — this bead is
a precondition for trusting that backend in production.

## Dependency rationale
Depends on construct-b0nny.3 (built) and construct-b0nny.12 (the CTE-hang fix, must land first
so the exposed CLI commands don't ship a known-hanging query path).

issues.description:
## Objective
Design and build directive §17's E2 outcome: the Workspace domain model and its durable storage
— the concrete data model for "Workspace" (target concept 1) as a first-class, persisted entity,
distinct from the ad hoc project-identity/state-root mechanics M1 converges.

## Desired outcome
A Workspace is a durable, queryable entity (owner, membership, settings, linked sources,
lifecycle) with real storage — not just an identity key (M1) but a full domain object other
epics (E3 planning, E7 shared server, E8 tracker projection) can depend on.

## Locked architectural decision
None yet — this bead's first deliverable is the design itself, following the same single-strong-
lead, no-fan-out discipline the program used for target-model.md and graph-store-design.md
(routing-plan.md WS3b/WS5 precedent). Do not fan this out; a strong lead designs the schema, then
builds it.

## Requirements
1. Define the Workspace domain schema (fields, lifecycle states, relationships to Source,
   Directive, Policy — target-model.md concepts 1-7).
2. Choose and build durable storage (SQLite embedded, Postgres shared — mirroring the pattern
   construct-b0nny.2/.3 already proved for the dependency graph, not reinventing a third storage
   pattern).
3. Reconcile with M1's identity convergence — Workspace id IS the canonical `deriveProjectKey`
   output, not a second identity.
4. Produce migration/versioning discipline from day one (the E1 lesson: unversioned inline
   schema was a real problem, per disposition-matrix.md C2 — do not repeat it here).

## Acceptance criteria
- A committed design doc (target-model.md-equivalent depth) citing target-model.md's concepts
  1-7 as its grounding, reviewed before implementation starts.
- A working, versioned-migration-backed Workspace store with CRUD + lifecycle transitions,
  covered by functional tests per CLAUDE.md's multi-component-feature rule.
- `construct doctor` and full unit suite green.

## Context
Directive §17 E2: "workspace domain and durable storage." target-model.md's concepts 1
(Workspace) through 7 already define the target shape at the concept level; this bead builds the
storage and domain logic behind those concepts.

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/target-model.md] concepts 1-7;
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/disposition-matrix.md] C2 (the
unversioned-schema lesson to not repeat).

New `workspace` node type in the dependency graph, if Workspace-level relationships need
graph-backed impact analysis (design decision for this bead's lead to make and justify).

above is made affirmatively.

## Impacted dependents
E3 (planning needs a Workspace to plan within), E7 (shared workspace server needs this domain
model), E8 (tracker projection needs a Workspace to project from).

## Dependency rationale
Depends on M1 (identity convergence — Workspace id must be the one canonical id, not a new
third one). Independent of M0/M2-M5 and E4/E5 — can run in parallel with those once M1 lands.

## Non-goals
Does not build the shared-workspace *server* (E7's job) or the planning logic (E3's job) — only
the domain model and storage those depend on. Does not touch the dependency graph's own schema
(E1, already built) beyond possibly adding a `workspace` node type.

build on it). Mitigate with the single-strong-lead design-first discipline (no fan-out) that
already worked for target-model.md and graph-store-design.md.

## Security
Workspace membership/ownership fields are the seed of any future multi-user authorization (E7) —
design with that in mind even though E7 builds the actual auth.

None yet — this is local domain modeling, no external effect.

## Implementation guidance
Do not start building storage before the design doc is reviewed — this mirrors the
construct-b0nny.2→.3 (design→build) sequencing that worked well in this program.

## Required capabilities
Read/Grep/Edit/Bash; strong architectural reasoning for the design phase.

## Recommended runtime and model capability
Strongest available reasoning model for the design phase (single lead, no fan-out); mid-tier
coding runtime acceptable for the build phase once the design is locked.

## Parallelization eligibility and rationale
Design phase: no fan-out (single lead). Build phase: internally parallelizable across schema/

One worktree for design, a separate (or the same) worktree for the build, off

target-model.md concepts 1-7; the graph-store-design.md pattern as a template for how to design
a new persisted domain concept in this codebase.

A design doc; a built, tested Workspace domain store.

Downstream epics (E3, E7, E8) depend on this bead's public API — define it deliberately, since
changing it later means touching three dependents.

Functional tests per CLAUDE.md's multi-component-feature rule (this touches domain model +
durable state); full unit suite; `construct doctor`.

None yet (new subsystem) — but must ship its OWN versioned migration discipline from day one, per

New, additive subsystem — no existing behavior to break; revert is a clean `git revert` if the

None.

New `lib/planning/` module (or equivalent).

Spike C's proven harness scripts; target-model.md concepts 8-9; the E2 Workspace domain model.

issues.title: Build the runtime-adapter contract, conformance suite, and replacement proof
issues.description:
## Objective
Build directive §17's E4 outcome: a runtime contract (general/Claude/coding/process-or-ACP
runtimes), a conformance suite, and replacement proof — generalizing spike F's one-adapter proof
into the real, multi-runtime contract the rest of the program (M4 org-metaphor, M5a model-loop)
depends on.

## Desired outcome
A documented runtime-adapter contract with a conformance suite any runtime implementation must
pass; at least the general/Claude/coding/process-or-ACP shapes named in the directive have a
conforming adapter; replacement proof (swap one adapter for another with rollback) is
demonstrated in production code, not just spike F's isolated worktree experiment.

## Locked architectural decision
Reuse spike F's proven swap pattern (build-beside, prove equivalence, config-declared rollback
seam, delete last) as the *process*, not a new one. The contract shape should generalize the
provider-adapter interface pattern already retained in disposition-matrix.md D1s
(`lib/providers/contract/*`), not invent an unrelated abstraction.

## Requirements
1. Define the runtime contract's interface (what a runtime must implement: invoke, capability
   query, health/liveness, cancel/interrupt).
2. Build a conformance suite any runtime adapter must pass (directive §11 F's "existing runs
   finish safely" property is one required conformance case — spike E's recovery findings
   directly inform this).
3. Implement conforming adapters for the directive-named runtime shapes.
4. Prove replacement: swap one adapter for another in a real (not throwaway-worktree) setting
   with rollback proof, generalizing spike F's result.

## Acceptance criteria
- The conformance suite exists and at least 2 real adapters pass it.
- A real (in-repo, not spike-disposable) adapter swap is demonstrated with a passing rollback.
- `npm run test:unit`, `construct doctor` green.

## Context
Directive §17 E4. Spike F (construct-b0nny.5.6) already proved the swap pattern works cheaply for
one well-isolated adapter (GitHub provider, gh-CLI→REST) — this bead generalizes that into the
actual runtime contract the model-loop migration (M5a) and org-metaphor cutover (M4) depend on.

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/spike-f-runtime-replacement.md];
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/spike-e-recovery.md] (the
in-flight-safety proof pattern, directly reusable as a conformance case).

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
Possibly a `runtime` node type if runtime instances need graph-tracked capability/impact
analysis (design decision for this bead).

## Expected edge changes
New `implements`/`conforms_to` edges if the graph-node decision above is made.

## Impacted dependents
M5a (model-loop migration hard-depends on this contract existing); M4 (Worker Profile's
`model_tier`/runtime selection reads this contract).

## Dependency rationale
Independent of M0-M3, E1-E3 — can start immediately, informed by spike F/E's already-gathered
evidence. M5a blocks on this bead's completion.

## Non-goals
Does not migrate `model-router.mjs`'s callers itself (M5a's job) — only builds the contract and
conformance suite M5a migrates onto.

## Risks
High — this contract becomes load-bearing for the model-loop migration, the single highest-risk
bead in the program (M5a). A wrong contract shape here compounds downstream. Mitigate with the
conformance suite as the hard gate any adapter (including the eventual model-loop replacement)
must pass before being trusted.

## Security
Runtime adapters are an authority boundary (what code/tools a runtime is allowed to invoke) —
design the contract with an explicit capability/permission surface, not an implicit one.

## Authority requirements
None for this bead itself (design + conformance suite); the runtimes it enables may need their
own authority scoping, defined as part of the contract.

## Implementation guidance
Start from spike F's proven pattern and the existing provider-adapter framework
(`lib/providers/contract/*`, disposition-matrix.md D1s) as the closest existing precedent — do
not design from a blank page.

## Required capabilities
Read/Grep/Edit/Bash; strong architectural reasoning for the contract design.

## Recommended runtime and model capability
Strongest available reasoning model for the contract design (single lead, no fan-out, mirroring
WS3b's "single strong lead" precedent for graph-schema design); mid-tier for conformance-suite
implementation once the contract is locked.

## Parallelization eligibility and rationale
Contract design: no fan-out. Adapter implementations: parallelizable once the contract is locked
(each adapter is an independent implementation of the same interface).

## Workspace/worktree ownership
One worktree for contract design, separate worktrees per adapter implementation.

## File ownership
New `lib/runtime/` contract module; individual adapter files under it.

## Inputs
Spike F/E's proven patterns; the existing provider-adapter framework as precedent.

## Outputs
A runtime contract; a conformance suite; ≥2 conforming adapters; a real swap-and-rollback proof.

## Integration contract
M5a and M4 depend on this contract's public shape — define deliberately.

## Validation
The conformance suite itself is the validation mechanism; full unit suite; `construct doctor`.

## Graph validation
`construct graph validate` if a `runtime` node type is added.

## Migration
None (new subsystem).

## Rollback
New, additive subsystem; the swap-and-rollback proof (Requirements item 4) is itself evidence
this bead's own deliverable is safely reversible.

## Deletion/cleanup
None.

## Completion evidence
Link the contract-design commit, conformance-suite results, and the swap/rollback proof.
issues.notes:
Implemented on branch bead/construct-b0nny.24, commit b5eae08202f6fb9024f8e48b1e21c53061dc00de (local only, not pushed/merged, per instructions).

CONTRACT DESIGN (lib/runtime/contract/):
- interface.mjs: validate()/hasCapability(), mirroring lib/providers/contract/interface.mjs's shape (disposition-matrix D1s precedent). Required surface on every adapter: name, kind, capabilities[], init(config), invoke(request, context), health(), cancel(invocationId). capabilities is drawn from CAPABILITIES=['interrupt','stream','sandbox','concurrent'] and declares OPTIONAL behavior (e.g. 'interrupt' means cancel() can actually stop in-flight work; its absence means cancel() is a documented safe no-op, not a missing method) — this is the explicit capability/permission surface the bead's Security note required.
- errors.mjs: RuntimeError/RuntimeNotReadyError/InvocationError/InvocationTimeoutError, mirroring providers/contract/errors.mjs.
- conformance.mjs: runConformanceSuite(fixture) — the shared suite, mirroring contract-tests.mjs. Cases: interface validation, name/kind, known capabilities matching declared interrupt support, invoke() rejects before init(), health() after init(), invoke() well-shaped result, cancel() on unknown id is a safe no-op, and (when the fixture supplies invokeSlow) the REQUIRED "an in-flight invocation finishes safely despite an unrelated cancel()" case — generalizing directive Section 11 F / spike E's recovery property into a hard per-adapter gate, plus a case asserting cancel() actually interrupts when 'interrupt' is declared and safely no-ops when it isn't.
- registry.mjs / default-registry.mjs: createRuntimeRegistry (register/resolve/has/keys) — the swap seam. default-registry.mjs wires 'general' (in-process), 'coding-claude' (CLI subprocess), 'coding-acp' (stdio JSON-RPC) as production defaults.

ADAPTERS (4 total, covering the directive's general/Claude/coding/process-or-ACP shapes):
- adapters/general/inprocess.mjs: in-process handler runtime, cooperative cancel via AbortSignal.
- adapters/coding/process-transport.mjs + claude-cli.mjs: real async-subprocess transport (node:child_process spawn, not spawnSync so cancel() can truly kill an in-flight call), specialized to shell out to the claude CLI. Generalizes spike F's gh-CLI subprocess shape from a provider transport to a runtime transport.
- adapters/coding/acp-stdio.mjs: process-or-ACP shape — newline-delimited JSON-RPC over a persistent stdio subprocess. Explicitly documented as demonstrating the transport family, not claiming conformance to a specific published ACP wire spec (no-fabrication).
- adapters/coding/claude-api.mjs: HTTP Messages-API transport (fetch-based) — the "after" side of the replacement proof.

REPLACEMENT PROOF (tests/functional/runtime-adapter-swap.functional.test.mjs):
A real (not spawnFn-faked) OS-subprocess adapter (node spawning node against a real script in an mkdtemp fixture) is resolved from a live registry, a slow invocation is started on it, the registry entry is swapped mid-flight to the HTTP-transport adapter, and the in-flight subprocess call is confirmed to complete unaffected by the swap (the registry-layer generalization of spike F's ESM in-flight-safety proof). A fresh resolve() after the swap picks up the new adapter; the registry entry is then rolled back and a fresh resolve() confirms the original subprocess behavior is restored exactly — the registry-level equivalent of spike F's git-revert rollback proof, done in this repo's own git history (not a disposable worktree). A second functional test confirms an already-held instance is unaffected by a later re-registration.

TEST RESULTS (real, directly observed, re-run and independently confirmed twice each):
- npm run test:unit: 574 pass, 0 fail, 73 suites, exit 0 (run twice, identical both times).
- My new test files run directly (tests/runtime-contract-{inprocess,claude-cli,claude-api,acp-stdio,registry}.test.mjs + tests/functional/runtime-adapter-swap.functional.test.mjs): 53 pass, 0 fail (51 unit + 2 functional).
- tests/functional/audit-ratchet.functional.test.mjs: verified via git-stash A/B comparison that this test ALREADY fails on the pre-bead base commit (ec050b6d) with 8 findings (postgres-store.mjs dead-code + 7 unnavigated workspace-control-plane doc dirs) unrelated to this work. My change initially added 3 MORE findings (lib/runtime/contract/{conformance,default-registry,adapters/coding/claude-api}.mjs flagged module-test-only, since nothing in production imports them yet — expected, since this bead explicitly does not wire callers, that's M4/M5a's job). Fixed by adding these 3 to scripts/audit/02-deadcode.mjs's ACCEPTED_TEST_ONLY allowlist with documented reasons (same mechanism already used for lib/providers/contract/contract-tests.mjs). Re-verified: only the same 8 pre-existing findings remain, identical to the base-commit run.
- tests/audit/f12-gates/audit-doc-staleness.test.mjs: this WAS a real regression I introduced (adding 6 new test files drifted tests/AUDIT.md's hard-coded corpus counts, 930 vs 936 files, 274 vs 275 functional files). Fixed by running scripts/generate-test-corpus-inventory.mjs (regenerated tests/AUDIT.md + tests/capabilities/corpus-inventory.json, now committed). Re-verified: 5/5 pass.
- Full `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` / `npm run test:functional` (~275 functional files): attempted twice in this session; both times the machine was under severe concurrent load from other parallel agent worktree sessions also running full suites simultaneously (uptime showed load average 15-25 with up to 26 concurrent `node --test` processes across worktrees at once) and the run did not reach completion in-session. The completed portion (376 lines / 306 passed / 1 failed, the same known pre-existing audit-ratchet finding above, zero other failures) showed no new regressions in what it covered. issues.title: Build the production sources/directives/workplace loop
issues.description:
## Objective
Build directive §17's E5 outcome — a production sources/directives/workplace loop — generalizing
spike D's validated detect→normalize→align→filter→gate→simulate→verify→no-fabricate scaffolding
from a fixture-driven proof into a real system that ingests real sources (GitHub/Jira/Slack-class
providers, already retained per disposition-matrix.md D1s) and drives real (approval-gated)
external effects through the M2 chokepoint.

## Desired outcome
A production workplace loop that detects real signals from connected sources, checks them
against real Workspace strategy/objectives (E2), proposes real artifacts, and only acts
externally after passing through M2's governed-write chokepoint — with the same no-fabrication
discipline spike D proved (a no-op run reports "nothing new," never invents activity).

## Locked architectural decision
Per spike D's own honest verdict: the scaffolding is conditionally validated, but detection
being rule-based over an intentionally-legible fixture does NOT prove judgment over messy real
data — that gap must be explicitly re-tested against real sources before this bead is called
done, not assumed away.

## Requirements
1. Reuse spike D's proven pipeline shape (detect/normalize/align/filter/gate/simulate/verify/
   no-fabricate) as the architecture — do not redesign it from scratch.
2. Replace the fixture sources with real provider adapters (already retained, D1s) for at least
   one real GitHub/Jira/Slack-class source.
3. Route all external effects through the M2 governed-write chokepoint (spike D only simulated
   this; production must actually gate through it).
4. Re-validate detection quality against real, messy source data (not a fixture built to make
   gaps legible) — report honestly if quality degrades, per spike D's own caveat.
5. Provide the equivalence tests M3b needs to retire Oracle's `directive-executor.mjs` onto this
   loop.

## Acceptance criteria
- The loop runs against at least one real connected source and produces a correctly-gated,
  approval-required proposal.
- A second run against unchanged real source state reports "nothing new" (the no-fabrication
  proof, now against real data).
- M3b's equivalence-test requirement (directive execution parity with Oracle) passes.
- `npm run test:unit`, `construct doctor` green.

## Context
Directive §17 E5. Spike D (construct-b0nny.5.4) proved the pipeline shape end-to-end against a
fixture and gave a conditional-go/no-go split verdict — this bead is the production
generalization, explicitly re-testing the part spike D flagged as unproven (real-data detection
quality).

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/spike-d-daily-workplace-loop.md].

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
Signal/proposal-related nodes if the loop's outputs should be graph-tracked for impact analysis
(design decision for this bead).

## Expected edge changes
New edges linking sources to detected signals to proposals, if graph-tracked.

## Impacted dependents
M3b's Oracle-daemon consolidation hard-depends on this bead's equivalence tests being green.

## Dependency rationale
Depends on E2 (Workspace domain — strategy/objectives to align against) and M2 (governed-write

issues.title: Build the shared workspace server (auth, Postgres, concurrency, deployment)
issues.description:
## Objective
Build directive §17's E7 outcome: a shared workspace server (auth, Postgres, shared artifacts,
worker claims, concurrent users, recovery, deployment image, Docker Compose) — the "team/
enterprise mode" deployment surface layered on top of the local-first product.

## Desired outcome
Multiple users/workers can share one Workspace's state concurrently via a server, backed by
Postgres (already partially proven — construct-b0nny.3's structural Postgres backend, hardened
by the E1-completion bead's live-Postgres proof), with worker-claim semantics preventing
duplicate/conflicting work, and a real recovery story if a worker crashes mid-claim (directly
reusing spike E's recovery findings, not re-deriving them).

## Locked architectural decision
None yet — largest, least-designed outcome in the program. First deliverable is a design pass
(single strong lead, no fan-out) before any server code is written, mirroring the
target-model.md/graph-store-design.md precedent.

## Requirements
1. Design auth (who can join a Workspace, what they're authorized to do — ties into E2's
   membership fields and M2's authority ledger, not a separate auth system).
2. Prove the Postgres backend under real concurrent load (builds on the E1-completion bead's
   single-instance proof).
3. Define worker-claim semantics (a worker claims a piece of work, another worker must not
   duplicate it) — reuse spike E's idempotency/stale-claim/supersession findings as the design
   input, since that spike specifically validated these properties.
4. Build the recovery story for a worker that crashes mid-claim, reusing spike E's harness
   pattern rather than inventing new interruption-point testing from scratch.
5. Produce a deployment image + Docker Compose per directive §17's own explicit requirement.

## Acceptance criteria
- A design doc reviewed before server implementation starts.
- Concurrent-user test: two simulated workers claim different work concurrently with zero
  duplicate execution.
- Recovery test: a worker killed mid-claim is correctly detected and its work either resumed or
  released, per spike E's proven properties.
- A working Docker Compose deployment.
- `npm run test:unit`, `construct doctor` green.

## Context
Directive §17 E7. Spike E (construct-b0nny.5.5) already validated recovery/idempotency/
supersession properties for a single-workflow harness against the E1 graph store — this bead
extends those properties to a multi-worker, multi-user server context, reusing the proof
pattern rather than starting from zero.

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/spike-e-recovery.md];
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/graph-store-design.md] (the
existing Postgres DDL this server will use).

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
None new to the dependency graph itself — this is deployment/server infrastructure around
existing domain models (E2 Workspace, E1 graph).

## Expected edge changes
None.

## Impacted dependents
None downstream in this program (E7 is a leaf outcome feeding only E9's final cutover).

## Dependency rationale
Depends on E2 (Workspace domain model to serve), M1 (run-store rebuild, for a real migration
story), and the E1-completion bead (a live-Postgres proof, not just structural mirroring, before
building a shared server on top of it).

## Non-goals
Does not change the local-first, solo-mode product — E7 is strictly additive (team/enterprise
deployment mode), per the directive's own "one product model across embedded and shared
deployments" standard (§18/§19) — solo mode must keep working unchanged.

## Risks
High — largest, least-proven outcome in the program; concurrent-worker correctness bugs are
exactly the class of bug spike E's harness is designed to catch, so lean on that pattern rather
than assuming correctness.

## Security
This bead introduces the first genuinely multi-user authorization surface in the product — auth
design deserves the same scrutiny as M2's governance chokepoint.

## Authority requirements
Auth/membership decisions should route through the same authority model M2 formalizes, not a
parallel one.

## Implementation guidance
Design first (no fan-out), then build incrementally: single-user server → concurrent-worker
claims → full auth → deployment image, each step gated on the previous passing its own tests.

## Required capabilities
Read/Grep/Edit/Bash; Docker for the deployment image; a real Postgres instance for concurrent
testing.

## Recommended runtime and model capability
Strongest available reasoning model for the design phase; mid-to-strong for implementation given
the concurrency-correctness stakes.

## Parallelization eligibility and rationale
Design: no fan-out. Implementation: auth, worker-claims, and deployment-image work are
reasonably independent once the design is locked and could parallelize.

## Workspace/worktree ownership
One worktree for design; separate worktrees per implementation stream once design is locked.

## File ownership
New `lib/server/` module (some of this may already partially exist — audit before assuming a
blank slate, per the program's own "verify before building" discipline that overturned Wave 0's
truth-map claims twice already).

## Inputs

## Outputs

proves unready.

None.

image build.
