issues.title: Build Beads tracker projection, field authority, and reconciliation
issues.description:
## Objective
Build directive §17's E8 outcome: Beads projection, field authority, reconciliation, importers,
and raw-record preservation — making `bd` a *projection* of the graph-informed work model (E1+E3)
rather than the sole source of truth, while keeping bd fully usable day-to-day (per CLAUDE.md,
still mandatory for task tracking).

## Desired outcome
Beads issues are derivable from (and reconcilable against) the graph-informed Work-spec model
(E3); field authority is explicit (which fields bd owns vs. which are projected from elsewhere);
existing bd data imports cleanly with raw records preserved (no lossy one-way migration).

## Locked architectural decision
None yet — design-first, single lead, no fan-out, same discipline as E2/E7. The existing lesson
already learned this program (`bd create --graph` is lossy; scripted per-issue create + `bd dep
add` is the safe path) is a direct input: whatever projection mechanism this bead builds must not
repeat that lossiness.

## Requirements
1. Define field authority: which bd fields (status, assignee, priority) remain bd-owned vs. which
   (dependency edges, graph-derived context) are projected FROM the E1/E3 models into bd.
2. Build a reconciliation mechanism that detects drift between bd and the projected source (not
   a one-time import — an ongoing sync, since bd is a live, actively-used tracker).
3. Build importers preserving raw records (every bd issue's full original data survives the
   projection, even fields the new model doesn't use) — no silent data loss, matching program
   rule 2.
4. Validate against this program's OWN bd history (construct-b0nny.1–.12 and this very bead
   program) as a real, non-trivial test corpus.

## Acceptance criteria
- A field-authority table (bd-owned vs. projected) reviewed before implementation.
- A reconciliation test detects an intentionally introduced drift and reports it correctly.
- Raw-record preservation proven against this program's own real bd issue set with zero data
  loss.
- `npm run test:unit`, `construct doctor` green; `bd` itself remains fully functional throughout
  (this bead must not break the tracker CLAUDE.md mandates for all task tracking).

## Context
Directive §17 E8. This program's own experience (`bd create --graph` lossiness, discovered and
documented as a standing lesson) is direct evidence for what NOT to repeat.

## Source evidence
[source: docs/notes/research/workspace-control-plane/synthesis/target-model.md] (concepts
covering Work/Plan/Assignment, whatever E3 finalizes as the projection source); this program's
own `bd` issue history as the validation corpus.

## Graph nodes created/modified/deprecated/deleted
None new to the dependency graph.

## Expected edge changes
None.

## Impacted dependents
E9's final cutover depends on this projection being trustworthy before any legacy tracker path
is removed.

## Dependency rationale
Depends on E1 (graph, done) and E3 (Work-spec model — the projection source). Independent of
E4/E5/E7/M0-M5.

## Non-goals
Does not replace `bd` itself or its CLI — per CLAUDE.md, bd remains the tracker; this bead makes
it a *projection*, not a replacement.

## Risks
Medium — a reconciliation bug could silently drift bd state from the graph-informed model,
producing exactly the "aspirational wiring" failure mode this whole program has repeatedly found
and corrected (roles/router, scheduler, legacy `.js` tier). Mitigate with the drift-detection
test as a hard gate.

## Security
None new.

## Authority requirements
None — internal tooling, no external effect.

## Implementation guidance
Validate against this program's own real bd data first (dogfooding) before generalizing to
arbitrary bd projects — a smaller, real corpus beats a synthetic one, per this program's own
repeated lesson about verifying against real data.

## Required capabilities
Read/Grep/Edit/Bash; `bd` CLI access.

## Recommended runtime and model capability
Strongest available reasoning model for the field-authority/projection design; mid-tier for
importer implementation once the design is locked.

## Parallelization eligibility and rationale
Design: no fan-out. Importer/reconciliation implementation: parallelizable once the
field-authority table is locked.

## Workspace/worktree ownership
One worktree for design; separate worktrees for importer/reconciliation implementation.

## File ownership
New `lib/tracker-projection/` module (or equivalent).

## Inputs
E3's Work-spec model; this program's own bd issue history as the test corpus.

## Outputs
A field-authority table; a reconciliation mechanism; importers with raw-record preservation.

## Integration contract
bd remains the CLI surface; this bead's projection layer sits behind it, not replacing any
existing `bd` command.

## Validation
The drift-detection test; the raw-record-preservation proof against real program history; full
unit suite; `construct doctor`.

## Graph validation
Not applicable (bd-side work).

## Migration
Existing bd issues (this program's own construct-b0nny.* history included) migrate through the
new importer with raw records preserved — an explicit test, not an assumption.

## Rollback
New, additive layer; bd continues working unmodified if this bead is reverted.

## Deletion/cleanup
None.

## Completion evidence
Link the design-doc commit, the drift-detection test, and the raw-record-preservation proof
against this program's own bd history.

issues.title: Rip out legacy daemon auto-spawn + ship legacy process/state cleanup sweeper
issues.description:
## Objective
Remove every path that spawns the legacy Oracle and Doctor background daemons, and ship a cleanup sweeper so existing installs (and the new release's postinstall/doctor) kill lingering legacy daemons and purge their stale runtime state. Maintainer directive 2026-07-18: legacy daemons must not run at all — v2 replaces them; nothing keeps them alive in the interim.

## Evidence (observed live, 2026-07-18)
38 leaked oracle daemon-entry.mjs processes accumulated in ~10 minutes on the maintainer machine during parallel worktree test runs. Root cause chain: functional tests run 'construct init' non-interactively in isolated tmp HOME dirs -> resolveShouldStartServices returns true for non-interactive -> startServices() calls startDoctor()+startOracle() -> heartbeat dedup reads the ISOLATED home (always empty) -> fresh detached daemon every time, outliving the test. Spawn surfaces: lib/service-manager.mjs startServices() (called by init-unified.mjs:1330 and construct dev), lib/oracle/cli.mjs 'construct oracle start', and lib/intake/session-prelude.mjs nagging users to run 'construct oracle start'.

## Deliverables
1. startServices() no longer starts Doctor or Oracle daemons (remove calls + results wiring).
2. 'construct oracle start' no longer spawns a daemon — clear removal notice pointing at the v2 replacement path.
3. session-prelude and doctor/watchers/oracle-liveness stop telling users to start the daemon (liveness watcher deletion itself stays in .17; here it just must not nag).
4. New legacy-cleanup sweeper: detects construct-owned daemon-entry.mjs / doctor index.mjs processes and stale runtime state (runtime/oracle heartbeat, doctor state, port-ownership records) and kills/purges them; wired into postinstall AND 'construct doctor'.
5. Functional test proving: (a) non-interactive 'construct init' in an isolated HOME spawns zero daemons; (b) the sweeper kills a planted fake daemon and removes planted stale state.

## Non-goals
Full Oracle entity deletion (directive-executor re-home, read-model consolidation) stays in construct-b0nny.17, gated on .25 equivalence. This bead only guarantees no legacy daemon ever runs and old machines get cleaned.

Legacy daemon auto-spawn ripped out (startServices/oracle-start/session-prelude nag/oracle-liveness watcher gone); lib/legacy-cleanup.mjs sweeper wired into postinstall + doctor.
